summary: The marketing team is in a critical push to finalize the knowledge website redesign and lock in fall event partnerships, while an unexpected Outlook lockout demands immediate IT triage.
summaryDetail: The most urgent issue this week is resolving the Outlook account lockout that has disrupted team access, requiring password resets across all devices and backend confirmation from JSB. In parallel, the knowledge website redesign is at a decision point: the team must provide final feedback on Joseph's HTML prototype and incorporate the agreed-upon features—BCI/BSI indices, a pinned article layout, and topic-based video dispersal—before development can proceed. On the program front, promotion is now focused squarely on Asia Start and Intelligent China, with US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) deprioritized for Q1; Joseph is finalizing Asia Start videos and translating the Marcom stats video, while the team audits conversion tracking to optimize SEO and AI search visibility. Looking ahead, CKGSB has committed to hosting UNICON 2028 and will participate as a free Knowledge Partner in the 2026 Sino-Swiss Economic Forum, with LIU Xuan tasked to prepare the host letter and review European Chamber speakers for immediate outreach. Additionally, the team should assess a potential meeting with Pulse (Germany) during their December China visit and ensure SwissCham email is sent and English case studies are shared to support these partnerships.

meetings.title: Knowledge Website Redesign Review
meetings.summary: The team reviewed two design versions for the knowledge website, comparing them to the current site. They liked the menu categorization and article page improvements but felt the overall design was too similar to the existing site. They discussed incorporating elements from Joseph's inspirational layout, such as displaying more articles and featuring indices, while removing the outdated video section.

meetings.title: Marketing Strategy and Program Promotion Planning
meetings.summary: The team discussed SEO and AI search visibility goals, prioritizing China-based programs (Asia Star, Intelligent China) over US partnerships, and reviewed conversion tracking setup for optimization.
